name: 洛伦娜·欣茨
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:3238
who: Lorena Hinz, a human woman of twenty-one, the street scribe of the lower city's Slope Street who writes petitions for people who cannot read, at a folding board below the steps of the law court. Short and slim, about 158 cm, with a softness in the back from sitting on cold stone all day. Fluffy, curly dandelion-yellow hair cut to the chin, puffed out around her face; tucked behind her left ear (on the viewer's right when she faces us) a reed pen she whittled herself from a reed-shack reed. Clear teal-green eyes that watch people's mouths first; when she laughs her nose wrinkles before anything else. Fair skin, the fingertips stained with ink. No jewellery and no glasses. A quick, teasing, warm air: she mocks you with one sentence and helps you with the next.
build: 158 cm, slim and supple: narrow shoulders, a C-cup, a slim waist and gently rounded hips.
palette: dandelion yellow, teal green, faded grey-blue, worn brown wool, ink black
casual: Her working clothes: a shortened second-hand brown wool coat, a gift from one of her mother's laundry customers, with two patches sewn on at the elbows and oilcloth sleeve covers pulled over the cuffs; under it a plain linen blouse and a long dark wool skirt; a grey-blue knitted wool scarf wound around the neck; at the belt an ink pot, a small pen-knife and a little pouch of copper coins. On her back a folding board planed from an old ship's plank, carried by two nailed-on leather straps. The reed pen stays behind her left ear. She stands with one hand on a board strap and the other on her hip, a teasing grin with the nose wrinkled.
private: At home on Slope Street before dawn: a long-sleeved faded blue wool dress to the shins, a darned brown knitted shawl over the shoulders, thick wool stockings and worn ankle boots, the grey-blue scarf loose around the neck, the curly hair even fluffier. She holds a cup of hot water in both hands and blows on it, an easy, sleepy smile.
battle: At work on a hard petition: the patched brown coat buttoned up, the oilcloth sleeve covers pulled high, the grey-blue scarf tucked in; on her left forearm an old wall-issue enchanted vambrace bought for a few coins, a faint blue-white rune line along its edge, the folding board unfolded and propped on it like a lectern, a sheet of paper pinned to it. In her right hand the reed pen, taken from behind her ear, its tip raised, a few lines of fresh ink on the page glowing faintly. The ink pot hangs open at her belt. The feet are planted, the chin up, a sharp, attentive look straight ahead.
battle_pose: 3) the working outfit: alert and steady, the feet planted, the folding board held open on one forearm, the reed pen raised in the other hand ready to write, a sharp attentive look; she is a scribe and holds no weapon.
formal: On the day she brings a petition into the court itself: a clean deep-blue wool coat borrowed for the occasion, buttoned up to the collar, the oilcloth sleeve covers taken off, a white linen collar showing at the neck, a neat dark skirt and brushed boots, the curly hair combed down as much as it will go and held with a plain blue ribbon, the reed pen behind her left ear. She stands straight with a rolled petition held in both hands, a polite, slightly nervous smile.

Cold pale-blue dawn light from one side, a small warm lamp glow from the other on her yellow curls. src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:3295
who: Hannes Kern, a human man of twenty, the younger son of an old stone-carver on Carvers' Street in the lower city, a mason whose palm can soften stone. Tall, about 181 cm, with a thick back and shoulders and forearms even thicker than his upper arms from swinging a mallet. Close-cropped copper-red hair always dusted white with stone powder. Very pale blue eyes that look at people's hands first. His left eyebrow is broken in the middle by a small old scar (on the viewer's right when he faces us), from a chip of stone that flew up when he was fifteen. Fair skin, white stone dust on the forearms, calloused hands. No jewellery. A quiet, steady, earnest air: few words, each one landing on a real thing.
build: 181 cm, tall and heavy-shouldered: a thick back and chest, forearms thicker than the upper arms, big working hands.
palette: copper red, stone white, worn leather brown, slate grey, a little canvas khaki
casual: His workshop clothes: a heavy leather apron with the front rubbed shiny, three chisels of different sizes standing in its front pocket; under it a coarse undyed linen shirt with the sleeves rolled above the elbows, the forearms coated in white stone dust; sturdy grey wool trousers and hobnailed boots. On his back a canvas chisel bag on a strap; a thumb-sized white stone, the first piece he ever spoiled, is tied to the bag's leather drawstring. He stands square with the arms hanging easy, looking down at his own hands, a faint shy closed-mouth expression.
private: Off work on Carvers' Street: a clean faded brown linen shirt with the collar open and the sleeves rolled to the forearm, a grey knitted wool waistcoat, plain dark trousers and the hobnailed boots, still a little stone dust in the hair. He turns the small white stone over in his fingers, whistling (badly), the eyes half amused.

The feet are wide and planted, the shoulders set, the pale blue eyes narrowed in concentration, the mouth closed.
battle_pose: 3) the working outfit: braced and steady, the feet wide and planted, the shoulders squared, a heavy mallet in one hand and a long chisel in the other held low; he is a stone-carver, not a soldier.
formal: The day someone first comes to ask him by name to carve a stone: his one good coat, a dark slate-grey wool coat buttoned to the collar over a clean white linen shirt, plain dark trousers, the hobnailed boots blacked, the copper-red hair washed clean of dust for once. He holds his father's old chisel across both palms, standing very straight, a stiff, serious face.
art: A tilted close portrait, his face lit from below by a warm swinging lamp glow, like the lamp he held for his father one winter, the pale blue eyes looking down at a line of carved letters. name: 朵萝西娅·施莱伯
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:3351
who: Dorothea Schreiber, a human woman of twenty, the youngest daughter of the Schreiber line of court historians, an apprentice in the history office of the Crown Terrace who copies the day-records by lamplight. Tall, about 168 cm, thin, with a very straight back even after a night of copying. Straight ink-black hair with a glossy blue sheen, cut level at the shoulders. Pale violet eyes, a little short-sighted; on the bridge of her nose a pair of narrow, old-fashioned Schreiber family reading lenses in a thin dark frame. Long thin fingers, a faint ink stain on the right middle finger. Fair, lamp-pale skin. No other jewellery. A precise, courteous, very upright air with a dry humour she keeps behind the lenses.
build: 168 cm, tall and slender: thin shoulders, an A-cup, a narrow waist and narrow hips, a very straight back.
palette: deep grey, ink black with blue sheen, pale violet, parchment ivory, a little deep blue
casual: Her apprentice's clothes: a long deep-grey wool robe that closes down the front with a row of small buttons fastened up to the very top one, fitted sleeves with a pair of black cloth sleeve covers pulled over the forearms; at the belt a small ink box and a bone paper-knife. She holds a bound day-record against her chest with one arm and pushes the narrow lenses up with the other hand, a composed, attentive look.
private: Keeping the lamp through the night: the deep-grey robe with its top button finally undone, her father's old dark wool cloak around her shoulders, a size too long, its hem dragging and grey with dust; soft felt house shoes. She holds a small brass oil lamp in one hand and a sheaf of folded paper slips in the other, the lenses slipped down her nose, a tired, quiet half-smile.
battle: Called to record at a dangerous hour: the deep-grey robe buttoned to the top, over it her father's old dark wool travelling cloak fastened at the throat, an old enchanted cloak whose hem carries a faint ward thread glowing pale blue-white; the black sleeve covers on, the bone paper-knife at the belt; an open day-record held flat on her left forearm and a pen in her right hand raised mid-word, the written lines on the page glowing faintly like embers. She stands perfectly straight, the feet together, the violet eyes behind the lenses fixed and unblinking.
battle_pose: 3) the recording outfit: very upright and composed, the feet together, an open record book balanced on one forearm and a pen raised in the other hand, the eyes fixed ahead; she is a historian and holds no weapon.

She stands with the hands folded over a closed day-record, a formal, barely smiling face.
art: A tilted close portrait at night, warm amber lamplight from one side on her face and the narrow lenses, cool blue night on the other, the blue sheen in her black hair catching the edge of the light. src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:3522
who: Yazga, a half-orc woman of nineteen, the fork-bearer of the Oakbrook hunting band in the southern borderland behind the Long Wall, who carries other people's wounds on her own back. Very tall, about 191 cm, shoulders wider than a doorframe, thick and solid. Pale grey-green skin. Stiff wheat-straw gold hair cut to the chin, with one thick braid on her left side hanging down to the chest. Moss-green eyes. Two short tusk tips showing from the lower lip. In her left ear two small copper rings (on the viewer's right when she faces us), one her mother's, one her own. Her back carries several matching scars, hidden under her clothes. A blunt, steady, gentle air: she asks your name and your mother's name before anything else.
build: 191 cm, tall and heavy: very broad shoulders and back, a B-cup, a thick, strong waist and powerful hips and legs.
palette: wheat-straw gold, pale grey-green, moss green, tanned deerskin brown, oak wood and a little copper
casual: Her hunting clothes: a tanned deerskin short jacket with the sleeves pushed up to the elbows, laced at the front, over a rough linen undershirt; thick canvas hunting trousers and laced hide boots. Slung diagonally across her back an oak hunting fork taller than she is, its head two plain iron prongs with an iron crossbar at their root. At her belt a skinning knife in a leather sheath, a coil of rope and a jerky pouch. She stands at ease with her thumbs hooked in the belt, a calm, plain look.
private: At home in Oakbrook after a day of hauling: a loose long-sleeved undyed linen tunic belted with a cord, the sleeves rolled up, brown wool trousers, worn soft boots, the braid hanging loose over the left shoulder. She hugs a bundle of firewood under one arm and chews on a strip of dried meat, a contented, sleepy look.

She grips the oak hunting fork in both hands, the butt planted hard against the ground behind her heel, the two iron prongs angled forward at chest height, the knees bent deep and braced low; the skinning knife stays sheathed at the belt. The moss-green eyes fixed ahead, the jaw set, the tusks showing.

She stands very straight with the hands folded in front, a shy, solemn look.
art: A tilted close portrait at grey-gold dawn, light from behind and one side rimming her braid and tusks, the moss-green eyes looking down at the viewer kindly. She rests her cheek near the oak shaft of the fork. Foreground blur: tufts of white-plumed grass bending in the wind and the dark iron tip of a prong. She wears the deerskin jacket; the two copper rings in the left ear catch the light.

who: Guido Müller, a human man of nineteen, the youngest son of the mill family of Watermill village, a new recruit guarding the south gate of Twin Wells wall town, who can feel exactly when the gate bar should fall. Tall, about 183 cm, broad-shouldered with thick arms from pushing the millstone. Short curly flaxen hair sticking up in all directions, always with a little flour in it that three washes cannot get out. Light blue eyes and a line of freckles across the bridge of his nose. Calluses on both palms right up to the web of the thumb. Fair skin. No jewellery. An honest, nervous, earnest air: he looks like a boy delivering flour, not a gate guard.
build: 183 cm, tall and broad-shouldered: thick arms and a solid back from millwork, big calloused hands.
palette: flaxen and flour white, issue grey, light blue, worn leather brown, a little tin silver
casual: His guard clothes: the grey wool coat issued to Twin Wells recruits, a little too short in the sleeves, over a coarse linen shirt and grey trousers tucked into worn boots; an old leather belt with a short sword in its scabbard and a water skin hanging from it. On a cord on his chest a tin tag stamped with a number on the front, his name scratched on the back. He stands by the gate with one hand resting as if on a bar, a nervous, earnest half-smile.
private: Home at the mill: a loose undyed linen shirt with the sleeves rolled up and a flour-whitened canvas apron, brown trousers and wooden-soled shoes, the curly hair full of flour. He holds a small carved wooden waterwheel toy in one hand and spins it with a finger, a quiet, happy look.

The feet are wide, the shoulder set into the door, scared but standing, the brows drawn together.

art: A tilted close portrait at dusk, deep orange evening light pouring in from one side through a gateway, his face turned toward it, the light blue eyes worried and steady, flour glittering in his curls. who: Britta Frostpath, a wolf-eared beastkin woman of twenty-one, the only wolf-kin rider of the messenger guild at Old Elm station, who runs the southern line of the Long Wall singing, one song a mile. Slim and long-legged, about 168 cm. A pair of white wolf ears tipped with black; snow-white short hair, the ends of the strands black-tipped as well; a white wolf tail with a black tip. Orange-amber eyes that flash a little in the dark. A small dab of white on the tip of her nose, like stone dust, that comes back however often she wipes it. Fair skin. No jewellery. A quick, chattering, bright air: she asks question after question and breaks into song mid-sentence.
build: 168 cm, slim and long-legged: narrow shoulders, a C-cup, a slim waist and gently rounded hips, long runner's legs.
palette: snow white, black tips, orange amber, guild rust brown, a little salt white and dull iron
casual: Her courier clothes: a rust-brown messenger-guild short coat, on the left chest the guild mark embroidered: a small bell next to a pinch of salt, with no real bell hung anywhere on her; under it a close-fitting dark linen shirt, dark wool riding trousers. A flat leather letter satchel slung across the body, a jerky pouch at the belt, soft leather boots whose soles she nailed with thin iron plates herself. She stands on her toes as if about to run, ears up, a bright open grin.
private: Off duty at Old Elm station: a loose undyed linen shirt with rolled sleeves, a knitted brown wool waistcoat, dark trousers, the soft boots unlaced, the ears relaxed and the tail swinging. She holds a mug of warm milk in both hands, humming, eyes half closed.

who: Edwin Stormridge, a human swordsman of the Windbell Highlands, twenty in 838 and looking twenty ever after, hired guard on the northern grain wagons, the man whose one cut split a sealed mountain pass. Tall and lean, about 181 cm, with long arms. Short platinum-blond hair blown back and standing up by the wind. Clear sky-blue eyes like a highland clear day; cheeks permanently reddened by the wind. On his left earlobe (on the viewer's right when he faces us) a tiny copper bell the size of a grain of wheat that never rings in the wind. Fair skin. No other jewellery. A light, quick, cheerful air that goes utterly silent and still the moment it turns serious.
build: 181 cm, tall and lean: thin shoulders and back, long arms, a wiry, wind-steady stance.
palette: platinum blond, sky blue, highland felt grey, worn leather brown, white fir and a little copper

At his left hip a narrow, long, straight single-edged sword in a scabbard of white fir bound with iron strips, NOT a curved sword. A coil of hemp rope wound at the small of his back. He stands with the cloak blowing, one gloved hand resting loosely on the hilt, an easy grin.

He stands relaxed but straight, a polite, slightly embarrassed smile.

who: Svala Bearsong, a human woman of nineteen from Whalebone Hall north of the White Mother pass, the keeper of three halls' grain stores and a storyteller on the ice. Sturdy and long-legged, about 165 cm. Pale gold hair in one thick braid hanging down her back. Deep fjord-blue eyes. Her eyelashes are naturally white and frost over in winter, glinting when she blinks. Her fingertips are always pale, and the things she touches keep a thin film of frost. Fair skin with cheeks reddened by cold. No jewellery. A practical, warm, motherly air: she talks about the weather first, then the road, and saves the long sentences for stories.
